findings.evidence:
`OrderResponse.status` becomes `OrderResponse.state`; the old name is not
kept. The OpenAPI file is regenerated.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The field is renamed in place
findings.recommendation: The design's own context says "partners' integrations read `status` to know when to ship": on deploy, every partner calling `GET /orders/{id}` gets no `status` field (undefined) and stops shipping, with no warning. Use expand and contract: return both `status` and `state` with the same value, mark `status` as `deprecated: true` in `openapi.yaml` and keep `state` optional or both required during the window, announce a removal date, and remove `status` in a later change. Add to tasks.md a test that the response still holds `status` equal to `state`, and amend the spec's requirement so the deprecated field is part of the contract until its removal. The rejected alternative "keeping both fields (duplication)" should be revisited on these grounds.
findings.title: Public `status` field removed in the same release, with no compatibility window

findings.evidence: - Changed: The order's `status` field is now called `state`.
findings.recommendation: A partner reading this release note sees an ordinary "Changed" item and gets no instruction, while their integration reading `status` breaks. Mark the item **BREAKING** (or, with R-migration-1's fix, "Deprecated"), state what consumers must do — read `state` instead of `status` — and by when `status` will be removed.
findings.title: Release note does not mark the rename as BREAKING nor say what partners must do
